definitions.ask: Swap legacy crontab lines atomically via a temporary cron.retire: list that sync removes with the block?
definitions.why: Agents can't act after their own commit lands, and the Mac is often asleep

choices.label: Atomic, unattended cutover on athena and the Mac; legacy lines sit in the file until cleanup
No retire feature; manual cutover on athena and later the Mac, with brief skipped or doubled runs

definitions.ask: Should the Mac jobs adopt the staggered schedule and --retry-timeout 120 that docs/vault-git-sync.md documents?
definitions.why: The docs explain the staggering; the live table looks like accidental drift

choices.label: Stagger at :00/:05/:10 with --retry-timeout 120 as documented; changes what runs on the Mac
Keep today's three */15 lines with no retry timeout, and rewrite the docs to match

definitions.ask: Should cronrun write job logs to ~/.local/state/cron/<job>.log instead of the legacy /var/tmp paths?
definitions.why: Job-keyed logs are what cronctl logs and status can find on every machine

choices.label: One size-capped log per job under ~/.local/state/cron, read via cronctl logs; docs updated
Keep each legacy /var/tmp filename through a new optional per-job log: field

definitions.ask: Create a global reference memory note crontab.md making cron: data the only source of truth for cron jobs?
definitions.requested: Make sure agents have first-class support (i.e. easy ability to read/write my crontab on any machine from any machine) for this new and improved way of managing my crontabs.

definitions.ask: Add a one-line [[crontab.md]] cross-link to tailnet.md, since cronctl addresses machines by these aliases?
definitions.requested: Review the crontab_as_code_via_chezmoi.md file in the research sidecar repo for context and inspiration before planning. I agree with all of the requirements recommended in that research file
